questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study at the University of Paris for many reasons. One being the amazing cultural experiences Paris has to offer, another being it's central location in the middle of northern Europe and a third is the french language. You will need to speak the native language of your exchange city and be able to attend classes in this language, and as i already spoke a bit of french, it seemed like an obvious and enriching choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my semester in Paris for many reasons but the scholastic part of the exchange was not one of them. Maybe i have been especially unlucky, but as far as i can tell from the testimonies of former students, it might be a shared experience. I have run into every problem under the sun. I was prepared for the large amount of bureaucratic hoops i might had to jump through, but this was on a whole other level. I realize there have been problems, both with the dispersement of the Erasmus grant this year, and also with the international department at the University of Paris, but this semester has felt a lot like yelling into the void. That being said, Paris is an amazing city and i have been very lucky to meet some great people and friends outside of the University, which made the experience a lot better.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This was definitely not easy. I started the application process in february of 2021 as i was set to attend the fall semester of 2021. The international department at the University of Paris stopped responding in april of 2021. In my letter of acceptance i was told that my classes would start on the 1st of september, so i arrived in Paris accordingly, a few days before. I then received absolutely no information for the next few weeks, and was told that because of COVID, students without student ID's or no set appointments were not allowed to go to campus. Fearing i'd miss classes i wrote to every single contact i could find within the administration of the Humanities Faculty. All i was told is that i wasn't supposed to start before the 18th of september. I googled which campus i belonged to and went there, with no information, and 30 minutes before my first lesson i received my first email from an administrative person, telling med they'd forgot about me, that half my classes were unavailable, either moved to next semester, at this point already filled up, or were being held at the same time. I was sent a map and a good luck. I soon figured out that half of my professors didn't have me signed up for my classes, and after multiple tries, and almost two weeks passing, it was discovered that the university had accidentally inscribed me as a masters student instead of a bachelor student. All the information and help i was supposed to have acces to was supposed to be via the international department, who never answered and instead sent out a set email explaining that they were very busy, and could not answer emails. This went on from april until december.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any help, and had to almost beg for someone to look at my files and not just pass me along to another email chain with no response. I did have the fortune of encountering some very sweet and helpful people, working in the administrative hallway, and even though they didn't have the ability to access the systems to properly help me, they did go above and beyond to try and take me by the hand and help me out. I ended up changing almost all of my courses. Thankfully the individual professors who taught these other courses were very helpful, in trying to help me catch up on the weeks of missed classes, creating dropboxes for me and sending me instructions, as i did not gain access to the online portal of the school until the beginning of december, more than three months into four month exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: This was extremely frustrating. I am in my mid twenties and have been lucky to travel quite a bit, which luckily prepared me for this, but i felt completely stranded. The amount of bureaucracy i have encountered and the multiple, multiple systems you have to coordinate with is astounding. I have had a very lovely councilor at home at KU, who tried to help me as best as she could, but there is only so much you can do from a different country. I realize that this semester might have been different because of COVID, but none of the systems that were supposed to be in place, were available. The "buddy" system, which is offered, i never heard back from, LANSAD, the french course available to exchange students, never in four months answered, even though i spoke to them in person and the recreational activities, study groups and international events never happened.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that bad. I found hosing through an ad on the Danish Church of Paris, and was very happy with the studio i received. Paris is ofcourse expensive, but it is manageable if you find a place with a somewhat cheap rent. I will recommend joining every single facebook group about housing in paris, international students, erasmus students in paris and so on, to try and find rentals!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: i would definitely recommend living off campus! From the experience of other exchange students i talked to, they did live very cheap, around 300-350€ a month, which is almost unprecedented in Paris, they did live pretty far away from the city center, in the outskirts of Paris, and often in typical dorm rooms in very classic scandinavian style, as we know them from dorms in Copenhagen. If you want the classic Parisian feel, i'd definitely try and search for a studio. Remember to get a real renters contract, as you might need it for later! Also take photos of absolutely everything in your apartment, room the day you arrive and inform your landlord that you have done this. So many people i met in Paris have been scammed by landlords, who banks on you staying for a semester, going home and then not following up. Also; if they ask you to pay rent in cash, ask for a receipt for the transaction!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found off campus housing myself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the process in itself alright. When all the other administrative problems were fixed, i was directed to another coordinator who within a few days sent me the course program and had me signed up for them within the weeks end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had already registered for classes before the exchange began, but was more than prepared to find new classes upon arrival as i heard this was the norm. However i was not inscriped at the university at all, and in the process of figuring out why, and how it would be possible for me to achieve just the right amount of ECTS-points, without having to attend two classes at the same time, i did miss a few weeks of classes, which i had to make up for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know what kind of help was available. I asked a security guard for an administrative floor, handed in my passport in return for a guest pass, as i did not receive a student ID, and simply knocked on every single door i could find.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was somewhat succesfull. By the time i was supposed to enroll in new classes, as it was discovered that the classes i had signed up for weren't available, the semester had already started and i more or less had to pick whichever classes would fit into my scheme and had the room for extra students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend to print out every single document pertaining to your exchange before you leave Denmark and bring it around with you everywhere. This was my only saving grace, as i had the proof that i had been accepted and was supposed to be enrolled, when they could not locate me in their systems. Otherwise id recommend to not quit. I called everyone, emailed everyone and eventually just showed up and knocked on the office doors. Ofcourse, being respectful, tactful and appreciative of the administrative staff's hard work and following up with them is very helpful as well!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes at University of Paris are very different from classes at KU. I think this might be a cultural difference and due to the age gap. Most Parisian students finish Lycée, their highschool at age 17, and go directly to university, so they are a fair bit younger. most of the teaching is also mostly based on the teacher teaching "at" the class, without the need for many class discussion or student participation.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to compare the level of courses as it is very different from the courses at KU. There is definitely less reading material at home, but also more in class hours. To obtain 30 ECTS for a semester, it would mean that i attended classes five days a week for three hours a day.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found that this varied greatly from professor to professor. I would say that in general, it closer resembles the style of classes at a gymnasium in Denmark, where you are taught a subject, maybe listen to a podcast in class, and then fill out a sheet of paper with questions pertaining to the lecture. All of my courses were classroom-courses and not in a lecture hall.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
British history: Public History and Popular history.
American Renaissance: Literary transmutations from 17th century England to 19th century America.
Literature: Language Games.
Visual Arts: The Body on Screen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think i would recommend most of my courses. I especially enjoyed British History, as it gave a thorough look at the perception of public history and memory from the 1850's-present time. All of my professors were very kind and helpfull and tought fascinating subjects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Personally i rented a bike for my entire stay, through Swapfiets, which was very affordable public transportation. I encountered unexpected costs pertaining to my phone company. I have unlimited usage in Europe, which was supposed to work exactly like at home, but apparently that is only up until a certain amount of months have been spend abroad, so i had to buy a sim card with a french number for the last week of my stay. Grocery shopping can be surprisingly easy depending on the supermarket. Overall, not many unexpected costs, though it in general is a very expensive city for a student.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery is very cheap if you visit Carrefour or Lidl! Public transport can be extremely expensive, if you plan on signing for a metro card. I would not recommend this, but i generally also just walked or bought single use tickets (which are good for over an hour!) or i biked. You can take out a 0€ a month velib card, which in turn costs 1€ per first half an hour and 2€ for an hour. This is very practical when moving around the city, as all metros close at night! I did not have to buy any books, as the university provided the need excerpts online. Eating out is also very expensive in general, so look around the city for cheap eateries! Also, if you're a student, or a european union resident under 26, almost all museums (although not all galleries) are free!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had hoped to engage in social activities or recreational sport at the host institution, but due to administrative mix-ups, i never got the chance.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware, as i didn't use these.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Despite all my administrative problems, Paris is an amazing city! I would highly recommend going to museums and visiting all the cultural institutions that are situated around the city. Also, i would recommend walking around as much as you can! Visit the green areas situated around Paris, engage in social opportunities you can find online for exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting away from the very touristy areas such as Marais or Montmartre. Generally everything is more affordable when you leave the first 10 arrondissements. I'd also recommend Les Puces, europes largest antique market situated at Port de Clignangourt in the 18th arrondissement.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was somehow easy. Although i will say that there is a prevailing culture in Paris, at least when you live there, that you are expected to speak fluent french. I've run into many logistic situations in supermarkets, postoffices, office depots, where i've been waved away, because they found my french insufficient. Other than that, it is very similar to the culture in Copenhagen. Although, beware of moving around in traffic. I had all the arrogance of someone who has biked in Copenhagen all of my life, but you NEED insurance, as the rules of the road are non existent and confusing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had very little socialisation with students at my institution. I had nice encounters with other students when working in groups, but i think the 6-7 year age gap, definitely played a part. Also the social gatherings, which were advertised ahead of time, weren't really existing. I went to a "welcome-day" for erasmus students at the end of october, over halfway through my stay and met some very nice Erasmus students from all over the world.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challengin.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I greatly appreciated the social culture pertaining to social outings. Going out to eat or for a drink, people are very open and inviting and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Really consider if you want it. You have to work hard for it both before, during and after.
2. Have patience and persistence. You simply cannot automatically assume that you will get the information that you need, as is the case at KU. It is your responsibility if you want to get any information and get the classes you want. 
3. Socialize! Try and attend all the social gatherings you can. I think i counted on some inclusion into some sort of social relation with other exchange students or some university orchestrated gatherings for students, which was not the case. Try and meet people outside the host university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Unviersity of Paris have recently merged all their different departments into one large university with different campuses and branches. According to both faculty and students i met at the university, this has resulted in a massive hole in communication, and none of the branches are able to communicate within themselves, or have direct access to the many systems that are in place. This means that the staff at the Campus of humanities have no way of reaching the international department or other departments. You will need to physically go to the different campuses and offices and appeal to the different coordinators.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Paris. Just experiencing the culture of a major european capital. It is extremely hectic, with so much noise, so many smells, an incredible amount of people and a thousand new tastes. It was very rewarding to be able to experience all of this first hand, and in spite of all the bureaucratic troubles, i feel very privileged to have been able to experience this cultural journey.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative problems greatly soured the experience. I constantly felt i had to catch up on all my courses. The economical aspect was also very troublesome. I understand that there have been some problems with the dispersement of the Erasmus grant due to some troubles in the European commision, but this meant that i had the first installment of my Erasmus grant (70%) dispersed at the beginning of december. Less than three weeks before my classes ended and i was due to travel home for the holidays, and after more than three months spend in Paris. As many european cities, Paris is very expensive and my rent alone took up almost of my SU. This was very problematic and left me stranded, high and dry, with no means of providing for myself on my exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, i have enjoyed my experience abroad. But that is also something im able to enjoy in hindsight. I spend many days in hysterics, calling the international department at KU, trying to get some help, both with my new pre-approval, having my courses approved, trying to make sure everything pertaining to my Erasmus Grant would be accepted. I am very privileged and have been able to borrow money for the first three months, where the grant was not dispersed, but to someone else, who might not have these privileges, you would essentially been stranded, or would have to put yourself into debt. The saving grace of all of this have been the amazing city in itself, it's countless cultural offers, and the very helpfull professors at the faculty of humanities, who went above and beyond to help send me files, information and courseplans, when i did not have access to them otherwise.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
